title: Integral Nakayama for constructible internal modules
statement: Let ℓ be prime, E a normed field with a normed ℚ_ℓ-algebra structure, and X a scheme with noetherian underlying space. An internal module M over the continuous integral coefficient ring of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients] which is constructible in the library sense and on which multiplication by ℓ is invertible is zero. No finite dimensionality of E is required.

proof.text: Apply the existing proved private freeEpiLocalSplitting theorem in CondensedConstructibleSerre, attached to the local splitting node. The same module provides its regular-module inverse-image comparison. No local splitting proof is copied.

For a finite presentation, write π:R^n→M for the cokernel epimorphism. Pull it back along t=π followed by the inverse of multiplication by ℓ. The resulting epimorphism onto R^n splits locally by the preceding lemma; the first projection supplies T with Tπ=t. Then (1−ℓT)π=0. The proved contractive finite-free assertion makes 1−ℓT invertible, forcing π=0. As π is epi, the restricted M is zero.

Choose the finite stratification and the local finite presentation covers supplied by constructibility. The coefficient pullback ring comparison identifies their coefficient rings with the actual continuous integral rings. Exact additive pullback preserves invertibility of multiplication by ℓ. Apply the preceding finite-presentation argument on each member of each cover. Pro-etale cover restrictions detect zero, so each stratum restriction is zero.

Apply the existing proved private abDetectMaps theorem in ProEtaleAbelianClosedSupport to detect zero across the finite strata, using the identity map of M. The theorem uses inverse-image Kan extension, sheafification and quasi-compact joint surjectivity; no public closed-support assertion is applied. Each stratum immersion has the required quasi-compactness since its domain is noetherian.

proof_origin.note: Fully proved.
